test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If A varies directly as B, and A = 210 when B = 51, then find A when B = 136.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **A varies directly as B**, the ratio **A/B** remains **constant**.

Direct proportion logic: A₁ ÷ B₁ = A₂ ÷ B₂

210 ÷ 51 = A₂ ÷ 136

A₂ = (210 × 136) ÷ 51 = 210 × (8 ÷ 3) × 1 = 70 × 8 = 560

**∴ The correct answer is 560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A ∝ B, A₁ = 210, B₁ = 51, B₂ = 136.

**Formula Used:** A = k × B, where **k** is the **constant of proportionality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dbf17e143355fcf2d329991d42aefe5817d97f4eb2433b802990a4785bce698.png] 

⇒ 210 = k × 51

⇒ k = 210 ÷ 51 = 70 ÷ 17

⇒ A = (70 ÷ 17) × 136

⇒ A = 70 × 8

⇒ A = 560

**∴ The correct answer is 560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When one quantity increases, the other increases in the same ratio. Formula: y = kx or y₁/x₁ = y₂/x₂.

Inverse Variation

When one quantity increases, the other decreases in the same ratio. Formula: xy = k or x₁y₁ = x₂y₂.

Constant of Proportionality

The fixed ratio 'k' between two proportional quantities that defines their relationship.</p
